He mistakes her limited experience and directness for an unspoiled nature, while she mistakes his name and social ease for wealth. They marry despite the doubts of people who understand how little they know about each other. Ralph hopes for companionship and a settled family life; Undine expects travel, clothes, entertainment, and immediate access to the richest people around them. The mismatch becomes apparent as bills mount. She is increasingly interested in Peter Van Degen, whose fortune allows the conspicuous pleasures Ralph cannot provide, and she resents every appeal to economy as a personal deprivation.

Ralph struggles to support Undine's spending while trying to preserve his literary hopes. Their son Paul does not hold Undine's attention for long, and care of the child falls mainly to the Marvell family. Undine travels and places herself in Peter Van Degen's company, treating his interest as a possible escape from her disappointing marriage. Ralph at first tries to trust her, but her absences and contempt make the marriage untenable. Undine seeks a divorce in a jurisdiction willing to grant one and expects Peter to marry her afterward. Instead, once she is free and the pursuit has lost its excitement, Peter withdraws, leaving her socially exposed and without the richer marriage she had assumed would follow.

Living abroad after the failure of her plan with Peter, Undine looks for another route upward. She attracts Raymond de Chelles, whose title and ancient family offer a kind of prestige unavailable in New York. Religious and legal barriers to their marriage require her personal history to be examined. Meanwhile Ralph tries to secure the return of Paul. He learns that Undine had once married Elmer Moffatt in Apex and had kept that marriage hidden. The revelation destroys Ralph's remaining hope and compounds his financial and emotional exhaustion. He dies by suicide, leaving Paul subject to arrangements made by Undine and the surviving family. Undine is then able to move toward marriage with Raymond.

As the Marquise de Chelles, Undine possesses a title and a place in an old French family, but daily life at the family estate frustrates her. Raymond treats inherited land, customs, and possessions as trusts to be preserved. Undine sees restrictions, inadequate spending money, and exclusion from the more mobile international society she prefers. Their conflict concentrates on valuable family tapestries that she wants converted into cash and Raymond refuses to sell. Elmer Moffatt reappears transformed into a powerful financier and collector. His success makes him attractive to Undine in a way he was not when she was trying to erase Apex, and he has both the money and the flexible values her present marriage lacks.

Undine decides to leave Raymond for Moffatt. She secretly turns the ancestral tapestries into the money needed to overcome the obstacles to divorce, despite having assured Raymond that she would preserve them for the boy. She marries Moffatt, whose immense wealth finally gives her unrestricted luxury and public display, and Paul joins their household. The boy enters their lavish home and recognizes the Chelles tapestries, exposing how completely family attachments have been turned into negotiable property. Even at the height of her material success, Undine is not content. Learning that her marital history prevents her from becoming an ambassador's wife, she begins longing for precisely that unavailable honor, and her cycle of desire continues.

characters.description: A Harvard professor of religious symbology visiting Paris, an authority on secret societies, sacred iconography, and hidden meaning in art. Called to a crime scene late at night, he finds himself a suspect and is drawn into a frantic hunt through France, decoding clues concealed in famous works of art and history. Learned and level-headed, he pieces together riddles under relentless pursuit.
characters.name: Robert Langdon

characters.description: A talented French police cryptographer who warns Langdon that he is in danger and helps him escape. Quick, resourceful, and estranged from her family by an old rift, she has a personal connection to the murdered man that pulls her into the mystery. Her code-breaking skill and cool nerve make her Langdon's essential partner.
characters.name: Sophie Neveu

characters.description: The revered curator of the Louvre, murdered in the museum at the opening of the story. In his final minutes he arranges his body and leaves behind a series of cryptic clues and codes. His death, and the strange messages surrounding it, launch the entire chase and hint at secrets he had guarded.
characters.name: Jacques Sauniere

characters.description: A stern, dogged captain of the French Judicial Police leading the murder investigation. Intense and devoutly private, he is convinced early on that he has found his culprit and pursues the case with single-minded determination, becoming a relentless hunter on Langdon's trail.
characters.name: Bezu Fache

characters.description: A towering albino monk and zealous, self-punishing devotee who carries out violence in the name of his faith at the direction of a hidden master he knows only as the Teacher. Scarred by a brutal past and fanatically devoted, he practices painful penance and believes he is serving God as he hunts for a long-buried secret.
characters.name: Silas

characters.description: A bishop who heads a conservative Catholic organization and serves as Silas's spiritual mentor and protector. Anxious about his group's standing within the Church, he is entangled in dealings with a mysterious figure and in the desperate search that drives the plot.
characters.name: Manuel Aringarosa

characters.description: A wealthy, eccentric British historian and Grail scholar living in France, an old acquaintance of Langdon's. Erudite, witty, and obsessed with the legend of the Holy Grail, he welcomes Langdon and Sophie into his estate and expounds at length on the hidden history he believes the Church has suppressed for centuries.
characters.name: Leigh Teabing

characters.description: The polished manager of a private Paris bank with a connection to the murdered curator. Protective of his institution's secrecy and of a particular safe-deposit account, he becomes caught up in the fugitives' flight as the chase moves through the city.
characters.name: Andre Vernet

recaps.ending: The mastermind orchestrating the murders is unmasked as Leigh Teabing, the affable Grail historian, who is the hidden Teacher. Obsessed with exposing the Church's secret, he manipulated the fanatical monk Silas, the bishop Aringarosa, and everyone around him, and he is willing to kill to obtain the Priory's guarded knowledge. His scheme unravels, and he is arrested by Captain Fache. Silas dies after being wounded, and Aringarosa, having been used and having lost everything, is left broken but repentant. The novel's central revelation is that the Holy Grail is not an object but a person and a bloodline: Mary Magdalene, presented as the wife of Jesus, whose descendants have been protected in secret for two thousand years. Sophie Neveu is revealed to be one of those descendants, the last of the line, and she is reunited with surviving family she never knew she had. Langdon deduces that the Grail, the sarcophagus of Mary Magdalene, lies hidden beneath the Louvre's inverted glass pyramid, where he kneels in quiet reverence at the close. The secret endures, protected rather than exposed, and Langdon and Sophie part with the promise of meeting again.
recaps.in_short: When the curator of the Louvre is murdered and leaves a trail of cryptic clues, Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon is drawn in as a suspect and flees through Paris with the police cryptographer Sophie Neveu, the curator's estranged granddaughter. The clues lead them into an ancient mystery: a secret society, the Priory of Sion, has for centuries guarded the true nature of the Holy Grail, which the story presents not as a cup but as Mary Magdalene, said to have been the wife of Jesus and the mother of his child, whose bloodline secretly survives. Pursued by police and by a fanatical monk killing on orders from a hidden mastermind called the Teacher, Langdon and Sophie decode riddles hidden in art and history with the help of the Grail scholar Leigh Teabing. Teabing is revealed to be the Teacher, willing to kill to force the secret into the open, and he is arrested. The monk Silas dies, and the bishop who backed him is undone. Most startling of all, Sophie herself is revealed to be a living descendant of the sacred bloodline, and the Grail's resting place is finally located beneath the Louvre.

recaps.text: Robert Langdon, a Harvard professor of religious symbology, is a recurring figure whose expertise in secret societies and hidden iconography has previously drawn him into a dangerous, widely publicized ordeal that made him something of a public name. In this loosely connected new adventure he arrives in Paris on ordinary academic business, once again an outsider whose knowledge of symbols and history will pull him into a deadly mystery.

Late at night in Paris, the curator of the Louvre is murdered inside the museum, and before he dies he leaves behind a set of strange, coded messages. Robert Langdon, in the city to give a lecture, is roused and brought to the scene by the French police, only to realize he is being treated as a suspect. A police cryptographer, Sophie Neveu, secretly warns him of the danger and helps him slip away, and the two set off to decipher the dying man's clues, beginning a frantic chase through the city and into a centuries-old secret.

characters.description: A Harvard professor who studies religious symbols and sacred art. While visiting Paris to lecture, he is unexpectedly called to the Louvre late at night to help interpret the strange scene left by its murdered curator.
characters.name: Robert Langdon

characters.description: The respected curator of the Louvre. Mortally wounded inside the museum by an attacker seeking a hidden object, he uses his final minutes to arrange an elaborate coded scene around his own body.
characters.name: Jacques Saunière

characters.description: A cryptographer with the French judicial police and Jacques Saunière's granddaughter. Intelligent, resourceful, and experienced with the puzzles her grandfather taught her as a child, she intervenes when she realises that Captain Fache has secretly identified Langdon as his murder suspect.
characters.name: Sophie Neveu

characters.description: The stern captain of France's Central Directorate Judicial Police. A devout Catholic known for forceful investigations, he brings Langdon to the Louvre and closely directs the inquiry into Saunière's murder.
characters.name: Bezu Fache

characters.description: A police lieutenant working under Captain Fache. He coordinates surveillance and field operations during the investigation at the Louvre and follows his captain's orders closely.
characters.name: Jérôme Collet

characters.description: An albino monk associated with Opus Dei who practices severe forms of bodily penance. Acting under instructions from a hidden caller known as the Teacher, he kills members of a secret brotherhood while searching for an object he believes they protect.
characters.name: Silas

characters.description: The head of Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation whose new headquarters have placed it under financial pressure and public scrutiny. He has entered a secret arrangement with a caller known as the Teacher and believes it will strengthen the Church and secure Opus Dei's future.
characters.name: Bishop Manuel Aringarosa

characters.description: A wealthy British historian living outside Paris, known for his lifelong study of the Holy Grail. Physically disabled and reliant on leg braces, he is witty, theatrical, and eager to explain his belief that the Grail tradition conceals a suppressed history of Mary Magdalene.
characters.name: Sir Leigh Teabing

characters.description: Teabing's French servant and driver. He helps manage the country estate and assists his employer when Langdon and Sophie arrive unexpectedly with the police in pursuit.
characters.name: Rémy Legaludec

characters.description: The president of the Depository Bank of Zurich's Paris branch. His institution protects clients through extreme secrecy, and he initially helps Sophie and Langdon leave with the item Saunière stored there before recognising how much risk they bring.
characters.name: André Vernet

characters.description: A nun and guardian of the Church of Saint-Sulpice who distrusts Opus Dei. Alerted that danger may be approaching, she watches Silas search the church and tries to warn the members of the secret group she serves.
characters.name: Sister Sandrine Bieil

characters.description: The unidentified caller directing Silas and dealing privately with Bishop Aringarosa. The Teacher claims to know the secret guarded by Saunière's brotherhood and coordinates the effort to seize its keystone.
characters.name: The Teacher

characters.description: The elderly keeper of Rosslyn Chapel in Scotland. She recognises Sophie and receives her with an emotion that suggests the chapel is the end of a personal search as well as a historical one.
characters.name: Marie Chauvel

recaps.ending: At Westminster Abbey, Langdon identifies Leigh Teabing as the Teacher who manipulated Silas, Aringarosa, and Rémy in order to obtain the Priory's secret. Teabing threatens Sophie and demands that Langdon open the second cryptex. Langdon has already solved its password, apple, and secretly removed the papyrus; he throws the empty cryptex, forcing Teabing to drop his weapon before the police arrest him. Silas dies after accidentally shooting Aringarosa, who survives and helps Fache understand that Langdon was framed. The final message leads Langdon and Sophie to Rosslyn Chapel. There Sophie discovers that the chapel's keeper, Marie Chauvel, is her grandmother and that her younger brother is alive. Her family was separated for protection, and Saunière raised her while concealing their connection to the bloodline attributed to Mary Magdalene. Sophie remains with her recovered family. Back in Paris, Langdon interprets the poem anew and kneels above the hidden chamber beneath the Louvre's inverted pyramid, where he believes the Grail rests.
recaps.in_short: After Louvre curator Jacques Saunière is murdered, he leaves coded clues for his granddaughter, cryptographer Sophie Neveu, and Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon. Pursued by police captain Bezu Fache, they recover a cryptex linked to the Priory of Sion and seek help from Grail scholar Leigh Teabing. He explains a theory that the Holy Grail concerns Mary Magdalene and a surviving family line rather than a cup. The pursuit moves to London as the monk Silas and a hidden mastermind called the Teacher seek the same secret. Teabing is exposed as the Teacher and arrested after Langdon solves the cryptex. Silas dies, while Bishop Aringarosa survives and reveals how they were deceived. At Rosslyn Chapel, Sophie learns that her grandmother and brother are alive and that her family was separated to protect its heritage. Langdon later concludes that Saunière's final poem points beneath the Louvre's inverted pyramid, where the Grail documents may be hidden.

recaps.text: Previously, Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon was drawn into a crisis at Vatican City after a CERN scientist was murdered and antimatter was planted beneath the papal conclave. With physicist Vittoria Vetra, he followed a trail through Rome that appeared to mark the return of the Illuminati. They discovered that the attack had been manufactured by the camerlengo, who sought to create a religious miracle and make himself the Church's saviour. Langdon survived the antimatter explosion, exposed the deception, and left Rome after the election of a new pope.

Louvre curator Jacques Saunière is attacked inside the museum by an albino monk named Silas, who demands the location of a secret keystone. Before dying, Saunière arranges his body and leaves a sequence of symbols, numbers, and messages. Police captain Bezu Fache summons Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon to interpret the scene but secretly considers him the principal suspect because one message names him. Cryptographer Sophie Neveu, Saunière's estranged granddaughter, interrupts the investigation and covertly warns Langdon that he is being tracked. She believes her grandfather intended them to work together. They escape Fache's immediate trap and begin reading the clues as a private trail based on codes Saunière once taught Sophie.

Langdon and Sophie follow Saunière's wordplay through Leonardo da Vinci's paintings and recover a key marked with a symbol associated with the Priory of Sion. Langdon explains that the Priory is said to guard an ancient secret connected to the Holy Grail. Elsewhere, Silas searches Saint-Sulpice for the keystone after being directed there by the people he murdered, but discovers that their instructions were false. He kills Sister Sandrine when she tries to raise an alarm. Silas is taking orders from an unidentified Teacher, while his patron Bishop Aringarosa believes their mission will protect Opus Dei and the wider Church. Sophie and Langdon use the key to identify a Paris branch of the Depository Bank of Zurich, where Saunière kept a secure account.

At the bank, Sophie uses the Fibonacci sequence from the Louvre as the account number. The safe contains a rosewood box holding a cryptex, a stone cylinder whose lettered rings must spell the correct password before a fragile message inside can be removed. Bank president André Vernet helps the pair evade the police, then attempts to take the box when he realises its importance; they escape with it. Langdon brings Sophie to the country home of Sir Leigh Teabing, a British historian devoted to Grail research. Teabing argues that the Grail is not a cup but a body of evidence concerning Mary Magdalene, her relationship with Jesus, and a surviving bloodline. He identifies Saunière as a leading member of the Priory and the cryptex as its keystone. Silas tracks them to the estate and attacks, but they subdue him as the police close in.

Langdon, Sophie, Teabing, his servant Rémy, and the captive Silas flee France aboard Teabing's private plane. During the flight they open the first cryptex and find a smaller one with a poem pointing toward a knight's tomb in London. The group evades the British police and visits Temple Church, initially believing its effigies provide the answer. The clue proves more complicated than expected. Rémy reveals that he has been working for the Teacher, frees Silas, and helps seize Teabing. The Teacher later kills Rémy and directs Silas toward an Opus Dei residence. Langdon and Sophie realise the poem refers not to a medieval knight but to Sir Isaac Newton, who was buried in Westminster Abbey, and they continue there to solve the final riddle.

At Westminster Abbey, Langdon and Sophie find that Leigh Teabing himself is the Teacher. Obsessed with making the Priory's supposed evidence public, he orchestrated the murders and used both Rémy and Silas while misleading Bishop Aringarosa. Teabing holds Sophie at gunpoint and demands that Langdon open the cryptex. Langdon determines that its password is apple, linked to Newton, removes the message unseen, and throws the now-empty device. Teabing lunges to save it and is captured by Fache's arriving officers. At the Opus Dei residence, Silas accidentally shoots Aringarosa and is then shot by police; he dies after learning the bishop will live. Aringarosa explains the Teacher's manipulation, and Fache finally accepts that Langdon and Sophie were framed. The recovered poem directs them away from London toward Rosslyn Chapel in Scotland.

At Rosslyn Chapel, Sophie meets its elderly keeper, Marie Chauvel, and discovers that Marie is her grandmother. Sophie's younger brother, whom she believed killed with their parents, is also alive. Saunière and Marie separated the children and concealed the family connections to protect them from anyone seeking the bloodline that the Priory associated with Mary Magdalene. Sophie is reunited with her surviving family and begins to understand why her grandfather guarded so many secrets. She and Langdon part after acknowledging their growing affection. Back in Paris, Langdon awakens with a new understanding of the final poem. He follows the Rose Line to the Louvre and concludes that the reference to a blade and chalice points to the glass pyramid and the inverted pyramid beneath it. He kneels above the hidden underground chamber where he believes the Grail rests, completing Saunière's trail.

characters.description: The last gunslinger, a lawman and knight-errant from the fallen land of Gilead, in a world that has moved on and is slowly coming apart. Hard, patient, and deadly with his revolvers, he crosses a vast desert in single-minded pursuit of the man in black, a chase that is only the first leg of a lifelong quest for the Dark Tower. He speaks little, endures much, and has trained himself to sacrifice nearly anything to keep moving forward.
characters.name: Roland Deschain

characters.description: A dark sorcerer whom the gunslinger has hunted across the desert for years. He travels always just ahead, leaving traps, corpses, and corrupted people in his wake, and seems able to bend minds and cheat death. Mocking and elusive, he lures Roland onward with the promise of answers about the Tower and the shape of the world.
characters.name: The man in black

characters.description: A woman who runs a saloon in Tull, a dusty desert town Roland passes through. Weary and lonely, she takes the gunslinger to her bed during his stay. She carries the town's fear on her shoulders, especially its dread of a local man the man in black had raised from the dead as a cruel trick.
characters.name: Allie

characters.description: A large, fervent preacher in the town of Tull whose revival sermons have whipped the townsfolk into a religious frenzy. The man in black passed through before Roland and left his influence on her, turning her fanaticism against the gunslinger.
characters.name: Sylvia Pittston

characters.description: A border-dweller who farms a hard patch of ground at the edge of the desert and keeps company with a talking raven named Zoltan. He gives the passing gunslinger food and shelter, and listens as Roland recounts what happened in the town of Tull.
characters.name: Brown

characters.description: A boy Roland finds tending the pump at a long-abandoned way station in the desert. Quiet and frightened, he has no clear memory of how he came to this world, recalling only fragments of another life in a great city and a sense that he died there. He attaches himself to the gunslinger, who grows to care for him even as the quest pulls them both into danger.
characters.name: Jake Chambers

characters.description: A spirit that haunts a ring of standing stones in the foothills below the mountains. It can seduce and devour a man, but it can also speak prophecy. Roland risks an encounter with it to learn what lies ahead on his road.
characters.name: The Oracle

characters.description: Roland's boyhood teacher in Gilead, a scarred, brutal master-at-arms who trains young apprentices in combat and discipline. In Roland's memories he is the harsh proving ground every would-be gunslinger must pass to earn his weapons and be counted a man.
characters.name: Cort

characters.description: A powerful sorcerer and counselor at the court of Roland's father in Gilead. In the gunslinger's memories he is a schemer who betrayed the household and helped push the boy, while still young, into an early and dangerous trial.
characters.name: Marten

recaps.ending: Roland catches the man in black only after sacrificing Jake, letting the boy fall to his death in the tunnels beneath the mountains rather than lose the trail. Face to face at last, the man in black reads Roland's fortune with a deck of picture cards, showing him figures that stand for the three companions he must draw to him and warning of the long road still ahead. He speaks of the Dark Tower as the linchpin that holds all worlds together, and of forces far greater than himself, then talks Roland through a night that stretches into what feels like years. Roland wakes much older, alone beside a set of bones, the sorcerer gone. Carrying his guilt over Jake and the knowledge that he must gather three to him, Roland walks west and comes to the shore of the Western Sea. The quest is only beginning: the man in black has pointed the way but given no comfort, and the gunslinger remains as driven and as solitary as ever, fixed on the Tower that stands at the center of everything.
recaps.in_short: The last gunslinger, Roland Deschain of the fallen land of Gilead, pursues the man in black across a vast desert in a world that has moved on. He passes through the town of Tull, where the sorcerer's meddling turns the whole town against him and forces him to kill everyone there, then finds a displaced boy, Jake Chambers, at an abandoned way station and takes him along. Crossing the mountains through dark tunnels, hunted by underground mutants and haunted by memories of his brutal apprenticeship in Gilead, Roland closes on his quarry. At the last he must choose between saving Jake, who is slipping to his death, and keeping his hold on the chase, and he lets the boy fall. He finally confronts the man in black, who reads his future in cards, foretells three companions Roland must draw to him, and speaks of the Dark Tower before a night-long talk ages Roland by years. He wakes alone and walks on to the edge of the Western Sea, still bound for the Tower.

recaps.text: In a world that has moved on, its old order broken and its lands turning strange, the last gunslinger, Roland Deschain of Gilead, crosses a killing desert in pursuit of the man in black, a sorcerer always just ahead of him. Along the way he stops at the farm of a border-dweller named Brown and, over food and shelter, tells of the town of Tull, where the man in black had lingered. There a preacher, Sylvia Pittston, had been stirred to fanaticism, and a dead man had been raised as a taunt and a trap. When the whole town, driven against him, tried to kill the gunslinger, Roland cut them all down, including the saloonkeeper Allie he had grown close to. He leaves Brown's farm and moves on across the sand, hardened and alone.

Nearly dead from heat and thirst, Roland reaches a long-abandoned way station and finds a boy there, Jake Chambers, keeping alive on the water of a working pump. Jake remembers little of how he came to this world, only broken images of another life in a huge city and a certainty that he died there. Roland, who has hunted so long alone, takes the boy with him. He half-suspects the man in black left Jake as a lure, but he cannot bring himself to abandon the child. Together they set out from the way station toward the mountains, where the sorcerer has gone.

Traveling toward the mountains with Jake, Roland stops at a ring of standing stones to consult an oracle, a dangerous spirit that can devour a man but also speak of what is to come. From it he draws word of three who must later be drawn to him, and hints of the road to the Dark Tower. The bond between the gunslinger and the boy deepens, even as Roland senses the quest may demand a terrible price. They press on to the foot of the mountains and begin searching for a way through.

Roland and Jake enter the mountains, descending through tunnels and following an ancient rail line on a handcar into the dark, stalked by the slow mutants that dwell underground. As they travel, Roland's memories return to his youth in Gilead: the harsh training under his teacher Cort, the sorcerer Marten's betrayal at his father's court, and the early, dangerous test that first won him his guns. The man in black stays just ahead, drawing them deeper toward a reckoning beneath the mountains.

At the end of the tunnels Roland faces a cruel choice: he can catch the boy Jake, who is about to fall, or keep his grip on the pursuit, and he lets Jake drop to his death rather than lose his quarry. Beyond, he finally sits down with the man in black, who reads his fortune with a strange deck of cards, foretelling the three he must draw and hinting at the vast design behind the Tower. Through a night that seems to last years, the sorcerer speaks of the size of the universe and the nature of the Dark Tower, then Roland wakes aged, alone, beside a set of bones. He walks on to the shore of the Western Sea, his guilt over Jake fixed in him and his eyes still set on the Tower far off across the worlds.

characters.description: The last gunslinger of Gilead, driven by a lifelong quest for the Dark Tower, the linchpin that holds all worlds together. Hard, disciplined, and deadly with his revolvers, he has already crossed a desert, sacrificed a boy, and been told by the man in black that he must draw three companions to him. This book opens with Roland alone on the shore of the Western Sea, soon gravely wounded and fevered, needing help to go on.
characters.name: Roland Deschain

characters.description: A young man from late-twentieth-century New York, quick-tongued, wry, and in the grip of a heroin habit, living under the thumb of his older brother and a mob dealer. Roland reaches him through a door that opens onto his mind, the first of the three the gunslinger must draw. Beneath the addiction Eddie is brave and clever, and the crossing into Roland's world offers him a chance at a harder, freer life.
characters.name: Eddie Dean

characters.description: A woman from 1960s New York, drawn through the second door as another of the three. Wealthy, educated, and active in the civil-rights movement, she lost her legs to a subway accident and uses a wheelchair. She is not, however, a single settled self: a hard and hidden second nature contends within her, and reconciling the two is central to her becoming whole in Roland's world.
characters.name: Odetta Holmes

characters.description: A respectable-seeming man of 1970s New York who is secretly a compulsive killer, choosing victims at random and pushing or dropping things on them from hiding. Roland reaches him through the third door. His past crimes prove tangled with the gunslinger's own story in ways that make him more than a stranger.
characters.name: Jack Mort

characters.description: Eddie's older brother in New York, who introduced him to heroin and keeps him close through a mix of dependence and guilt. Once Eddie's protector, he has become a burden dragging on his younger brother's life and choices.
characters.name: Henry Dean

characters.description: A New York mob boss for whom Eddie is smuggling drugs. Coldly dangerous and fond of building card houses while he waits, he runs his operation from a bar and expects his deals to go exactly as arranged, making him a deadly problem when Eddie's run goes wrong.
characters.name: Enrico Balazar

recaps.ending: By the end, Roland has drawn his three. Eddie Dean, pulled out of a life of addiction, has begun to get clean and is becoming a gunslinger in his own right. Odetta Holmes and her buried second self, Detta Walker, are forced into a single confrontation that Roland stages through the body of the killer Jack Mort, and out of it emerges an integrated woman who takes the name Susannah Dean. Jack Mort dies before he can be drawn as a person, killed by a train much as he once killed others. Roland remains physically diminished, having lost fingers to the beach-monster, but he is no longer alone: Eddie and Susannah, already drawn to each other in love, stand with him. The new fellowship leaves the shore of the Western Sea and starts inland, bound together as ka-tet on the long road toward the Tower.
recaps.in_short: Fevered and maimed after a monster on the beach takes two of his fingers, Roland finds three free-standing doors along the shore of the Western Sea, each opening into the mind of a person in twentieth-century New York. Through the first he reaches Eddie Dean, a heroin addict, and pulls him bodily into Mid-World after helping him survive a mob deal. Through the second he reaches Odetta Holmes, a legless woman whose mind is split between a genteel self and a violent hidden self. Through the third he inhabits Jack Mort, a secret killer whose old crimes maimed Odetta and once pushed the boy Jake to his death. Using Mort, Roland engineers a crisis that forces Odetta's two selves to confront each other and fuse into a single, whole woman, Susannah Dean. The three are drawn: Eddie and Susannah join Roland as the beginnings of a new ka-tet, and the fellowship turns inland toward the Dark Tower.

recaps.text: In the first book, the last gunslinger, Roland Deschain of the fallen land of Gilead, pursued the man in black across a desert in a world that has moved on. He passed through the town of Tull, where the sorcerer's meddling forced him to kill everyone, then found a displaced boy, Jake Chambers, and took him along, only to let the boy fall to his death in the mountains rather than lose the chase. Roland finally confronted the man in black, who read his future in a deck of cards, foretold three companions he must draw to him, and spoke of the Dark Tower as the linchpin of all worlds before a night-long talk aged Roland by years. Roland woke alone and walked on to the shore of the Western Sea, still bound for the Tower and now knowing he must gather three.

characters.description: The last gunslinger of Gilead, leading his new companions inland on the quest for the Dark Tower. Hard, patient, and deadly, he has begun teaching Eddie and Susannah the gunslinger's craft. As this book opens he is troubled by a growing madness: two contradictory memories of the boy Jake war in his mind, threatening to tear his sanity apart.
characters.name: Roland Deschain

characters.description: A young man from late-twentieth-century New York whom Roland drew into his world through a magic door. A recovering heroin addict, quick-witted and sharp-tongued, he has become a gunslinger-in-training in Roland's ka-tet and is in love with Susannah. He is discovering a talent for carving and for the deeper workings of the quest.
characters.name: Eddie Dean

characters.description: A woman from 1960s New York, drawn into Roland's world through a door and made whole out of a once-divided self. She uses a wheelchair, having lost her legs before she came, and is fierce, clever, and devoted to Eddie. She is learning the gunslinger's way and carries the strength of the hard past that shaped her.
characters.name: Susannah Dean

characters.description: A boy from a version of New York who once traveled with Roland and died in the mountains beneath the man in black's chase. His fate and Roland's memory of him have become tangled and painful. In his own world, a boy who feels he does not belong there is likewise being pulled toward Mid-World, and reuniting the two threads is one of this book's central aims.
characters.name: Jake Chambers

characters.description: A billy-bumbler, a small, clever animal of Mid-World that resembles a cross between a raccoon, a dog, and a badger, and can echo human speech. Gentle and loyal, he attaches himself to Jake and becomes a beloved member of the traveling company.
characters.name: Oy

characters.description: A sentient monorail train, the last of its kind, that runs across the poisoned waste lands from the ruined city of Lud. Vastly intelligent and dangerously unstable, it takes a cruel delight in riddles and offers passage only on terms that put the travelers' lives at stake.
characters.name: Blaine

recaps.ending: The ka-tet reaches the decayed city of Lud and, hunted through it, makes for the cradle of Blaine the Mono, a sentient and murderously insane monorail train. Roland's group is now complete: Roland, Eddie, Susannah, the redrawn Jake, and the billy-bumbler Oy. Blaine agrees to carry them across the deadly waste lands toward the Tower, but only as a game: the travelers must best the train with a riddle it cannot answer, or Blaine will speed into its terminus and kill them along with itself. The book ends on a cliffhanger, with the ka-tet trapped aboard, the poisoned lands blurring past, and a contest of riddles just beginning that will decide whether any of them survive to reach the next stage of the quest.
recaps.in_short: Roland and his ka-tet, Eddie and Susannah, follow the path of a Beam toward the Dark Tower. Roland is being driven mad by a paradox: because he changed the past, the boy Jake both died and never came to his world, and two memories tear at him. Jake, in New York, suffers the same split. The ka-tet draws Jake across through a haunted house and a speaking demon, and the paradox heals; along the way they gain a billy-bumbler named Oy. They kill Shardik, a great cyborg bear guarding a Beam portal, and press on to Lud, a ruined city torn between two dying gangs. There they board Blaine, an insane, sentient monorail that agrees to carry them across the poisoned waste lands only if they can beat it at riddles, and threatens to kill them all at the end of the line if they cannot. The book breaks off mid-contest as Blaine races toward its final stop.

recaps.text: In the earlier books, Roland Deschain, the last gunslinger of Gilead, chased the man in black across a desert, sacrificed the boy Jake to catch him, and was told he must draw three companions to him on the road to the Dark Tower. Reaching the Western Sea, and gravely wounded by a beach-monster, he found three doors into twentieth-century New York and drew two people through them: Eddie Dean, a young man freed from a heroin habit, and a woman whose split self was made whole as Susannah Dean. The two fell in love and became gunslingers-in-training under Roland's teaching. But Roland's meddling in the past has cut the thread that once brought Jake into his world, leaving Roland with two warring memories of the boy and a mind close to breaking.
